sections.h2: Where does a Jackson County seller take a signed deed?
sections.html:
Take the signed deed to the Register of Deeds at 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th Floor, Jackson, MI 49201. The county posts hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, with no lunch closure, and answers at 517-788-4350. Holidays the county observes are closed days.

Few sellers stand at the counter themselves, because the closing agent files the deed and pays the office. The transfer tax still comes out of the seller's side of the closing statement, which is why the counter's rules are worth a look.

Jackson County has 702 square miles of land, per Wikipedia, with the city of Jackson as its seat and only city. Villages include Brooklyn, Concord, Grass Lake, Hanover, Parma and Springport, with Cement City partly inside the line. A parcel in any of those places is recorded at this same twelfth floor office.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County counter charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
One flat $30 covers each document, whatever its page count. Jackson County's statutory fee page ties that to a change on October 1, 2016, and says $4 of the $30 funds survey monument upkeep. The authority is MCL 600.2567.

The county's fee page also lists smaller items you may run into:

  • $3 added for every further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges.
  • Copies of land records at $1 a page, with $5 to certify a document.
  • Name searches starting at $5, priced at 50 cents per year covered.
  • Tax lien name searches, state or federal, at $3 each.

Payment can be cash, check or card. Checks for recording go to the Register of Deeds. If transfer tax is due, the county lets you fold it into that single check.

sections.h2: How is Jackson County transfer tax worked out?
sections.html:
Two taxes apply, 55 cents per $500 to the county and $3.75 per $500 to the state, and the Jackson County transfer tax page lists both rates. Any part of a $500 step counts as a full step. The seller is the taxpayer under MCL 207.523, and the county's share is set by MCL 207.504.

The deed itself must show the total price. A valuation affidavit can stand in for that, and it costs nothing to file, but the deed has to mention the affidavit. Write any exemption you rely on onto the deed as well.

sections.h2: Are any Jackson County transfers exempt from tax?
sections.html:
Yes, and the lists differ between the two taxes. A deed given as security, a transfer under $100, and a spouse to spouse deed that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties are exempt from both. For the state tax, a deed from an owner to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild is also exempt, and so is a deed made through a mortgage foreclosure or in place of one. See MCL 207.526.

The county list in MCL 207.505 is shorter, so a gift to a son or daughter can escape the state tax while the county tax still applies. Phone the register of deeds with the exact deed type before the paperwork is signed.

A seller who paid on a deed that turns out to be exempt can ask the state treasury department for a refund.

sections.h2: Does my Jackson County deed need a treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
If it carries warranty language, yes, and the same goes for land contracts and their assignments with a warranty clause. The county treasurer first certifies the tax history that MCL 211.135 covers, five years back from the date of the deed.

Jackson County charges $5 for this certificate and wants it on a separate check payable to the Jackson County Treasurer, handed in with the recording. A quitclaim deed without warranties is excepted by the statute.

If tax is owed on the house, get a payoff figure from the treasurer early, and the title company will pay it out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What makes the Jackson County register of deeds refuse a deed?
sections.html:
Paper that breaks MCL 565.201 comes back unrecorded, and the county prints that statute on its Recordings page. Typical causes are layout slips and missing names:

  • Sheets outside the legal size range, faint ink, or type below 10 point.
  • A top band on page one that is under 2.5 inches.
  • A first printed line that fails to name the one event being recorded.
  • No printed name beneath a signature, a notary name on a different page from the notary's signature, or no grantee address.
  • No drafter's name and business address.
  • Unredacted social security numbers.

Per the county FAQ, a photocopy is refused because only original signatures qualify. Court papers need the court seal, and a death certificate needs the clerk's seal. Staff neither draft deeds nor sell forms, so hire an attorney or title agent for that.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about selling in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Owner occupants dominate here. QuickFacts lists 159,552 residents for mid 2025 and 69,801 housing units, with 75.0 percent of homes lived in by their owners. A household with a mortgage carries a median $1,377 in monthly owner costs, one without a mortgage $557, and the median rent is $985.

  • Middle home value, 2020 to 2024: $193,700.
  • Household income, middle point: $66,073 in 2024 dollars.
  • Residents aged 65 and up: 21.5 percent.
  • Density: roughly 228 people per square mile.

With over one resident in five past 65, sales that follow a death or a move into care come up often. A clean deed history helps those close, and the county records show it.

Geography matters to a few sellers too. Wikipedia notes that the Grand River runs through the city of Jackson and that the north branch of the Kalamazoo River begins in Hanover Township. A lot near either water course may carry easements or flood questions that show up in the recorded chain of title, so ask for a records search if yours does.

sections.h2: How can a Jackson County owner look up recorded documents?
sections.html:
An online grantor and grantee name search covers deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers, and heavy copy buyers can ask the office for an escrow account. You can also carry your parcel's legal description to the counter and staff will help you start a records search. Easement or lake right questions are often answered by the title insurance policy you got at purchase.

Owners can enroll in the free alert that reports any filing made under their name, a no cost way to spot a forged deed.

If a buyer raises a title question, pull together your recorded deed, the loan payoff statement and any lien notices. Those answer most of what a purchaser wants to see.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County recording fee go up with extra pages?
faqs.a: No. A long deed costs the same $30 as a short one. The only add on is $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Jackson County sale?
faqs.a: The grantor does. The recorder takes 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state on each $500 of price, unless the deed states a valid exemption.

faqs.q: Will Jackson County record a copy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. Only the original signed paper is taken. Court orders carry the court seal, and death certificates carry the clerk's seal.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim deed in Jackson County?
faqs.a: Usually no, since the statute exempts quitclaim deeds that carry no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts are the ones needing it.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Jackson County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Come Monday to Friday between 8 and 4, noon hour included. Legal holidays are days off, so check 517-788-4350 first.
